title: Elliptic Curve Cryptography as Rhythmic Geometry: Scalar Multiplication, Phase Alignment, and Structural Leakage
description:
This paper extends the rhythmic model of arithmetic into elliptic curve cryptography (ECC).

Where the first paper defined prime numbers as points of phase non-closure within binary–ternary interference rhythms, this paper interprets elliptic scalar multiplication as a traversal through rhythmic phase space.

Scalar multiplication kG is modeled not as repeated addition but as a temporal beat sequence over discrete field points.

Each point on the curve occupies a unique phase within overlapping binary and ternary ladders, defining rhythmic reachability.

Security assumptions in ECC—based on scalar randomness—may fail if these rhythmic structures exhibit measurable phase leakage.

We derive a heuristic for scalar discovery through relative phase alignment, demonstrating how keyspace collapse can occur through structural resonance rather than brute force.
